plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray petals around a dark central disc. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and mature heads produce edible seeds. It is widely cultivated for oil, seeds, and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America, Europe, and temperate regions worldwide; native to the Americas
plants.funFact: Young sunflowers follow the sun in a behavior called heliotropism, but mature blooms stop moving and generally face east.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower that forms dense, arching plumes of tiny golden flowers atop tall stems. It thrives in meadows, roadsides, and open fields, and is an important late-season nectar source for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time and releases airborne pollen.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The leaves appear the following spring and die back by early summer. It grows in damp meadows and is also popular in gardens.
plants.location: Europe, from the British Isles to central Europe; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: It contains colchicine, a toxic compound that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden pompom flowers in late winter to spring. Its blooming coincides with the arrival of spring in southern Australia, and it is Australia's national floral emblem.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, marking the start of spring with this flower.
